definitions.explanation: Describes a person or situation where things turn out favorably by chance. A common everyday expression using 運 (luck) + が + 良い (good).

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{運|うん}が{良|い}い。
{運|うん}が{良|よ}ければ、チケットが{取|と}れるかもしれない。
examples.english: If we're lucky, we might be able to get tickets.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れたが、{次|つぎ}のがすぐ{来|き}て{運|うん}が{良|よ}かった。
examples.english: I missed the train, but the next one came right away — I was lucky.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used in the conditional form {運|うん}が{良|よ}ければ (if lucky) and the past form {運|うん}が{良|よ}かった (was lucky). The opposite is {運|うん}が{悪|わる}い (unlucky).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {運|うん}が{良|い}いことに (fortunately; luckily)
- {運|うん}が{良|よ}ければ (if one is lucky)
- {運|うん}が{良|い}い{人|ひと} (a lucky person)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ラッキー: lucky — casual loanword, often used as an exclamation
- {幸運|こううん}な: fortunate — more formal
- ついている: to be on a lucky streak — colloquial
